primitives.name: Thermal Management Design
primitives.verbatim_quote: The circuit board may be designed with the intent of dissipating heat, e.g., by including thick conductive layers, exposed copper, heatsink, or similar.
primitives.assumptions: Heat generation from LEDs is managed via passive cooling mechanisms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overheating leads to reduced LED efficiency and potential skin irritation.

layer2.mapping: Thermal kernel derived from heat sink geometry and material properties to maintain safe operating range.
layer2.telemetry: Skin surface temperature and LED junction temperature.

primitives.name: Elastic Wrist Strap Fit
primitives.verbatim_quote: In addition to the elastic wrist strap, the design of the strap may allow for continuous micro adjustments (no preset sizes) in order to achieve an optimal fit, and a floating sensor module.
primitives.assumptions: Strap provides consistent pressure to maintain sensor-skin contact while allowing wrist flexibility.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient tension causes sensor slippage; excessive tension causes discomfort or occlusion.

layer2.mapping: Strap mechanics modeled as Hookean spring system ensuring stable sensor positioning.
layer2.telemetry: Sensor displacement and contact pressure variation.

The core operational principle of the wearable system lies in its ability to perform non-invasive cardiac monitoring using Reflectance Photoplethysmography (RPPG). This method relies on detecting changes in light absorption caused by pulsatile blood volume in the radial artery. The system integrates optical sensors with LEDs positioned to emit light into the skin, capturing pulse waveforms that correlate with heart rate. Thermal management is critical to sustain long-term operation without overheating, achieved through circuit board design incorporating heat dissipation features such as thick conductive layers and heatsinks. The mechanical design ensures reliable sensor placement via an elastic wrist strap that allows micro-adjustments for optimal fit and a floating sensor module that accommodates wrist movement. These primitives form a unified framework where physiological signals are captured, processed, and interpreted within a closed-loop feedback system for readiness assessment.
